text.title: django-pytest Core Rules
text.summary: Seventeen rules for the modern Django test stack on pytest. pyproject.toml settings, directory layout, shared conftest fixtures, and factory_boy pattern.

rule.statement: Use `pytest + pytest-django`. Do not use Django's `unittest`-style `TestCase` for new tests. Existing TestCase classes are migrated incrementally.
rule.rationale: pytest fixtures compose cleanly; setUp/tearDown chains do not. The ecosystem (factory_boy, hypothesis, syrupy) integrates with pytest, not unittest.

rule.statement: Test data is created in `@pytest.fixture` (in `conftest.py` or per-module). NO `setUp` / `setUpTestData` methods. Composition via fixture parameter lists.
rule.rationale: Fixtures are reusable across tests/modules without inheritance; setUp couples data to one TestCase subtree.

rule.statement: Test data is built with `factory_boy` (preferred for explicit factories) or `model_bakery` (preferred for terse one-offs). NO `Model.objects.create()` inline in tests. Use factory_boy DjangoModelFactory instead of fixture-as-function for test data. Override fields per test with UserFactory(email='x@y.z').
rule.rationale: Factories centralise defaults; bakery generates plausible values. Inline `.create()` produces brittle setup that breaks every model field change. factory_boy handles sequences and related objects; plain fixtures-as-functions require manual wiring for each variant.

rule.statement: Tests that touch the DB declare `db` (or `django_db`) fixture explicitly OR use `@pytest.mark.django_db`. No accidental DB usage. Mark test classes or functions with @pytest.mark.django_db only when DB access is required. Pure logic tests must not touch the DB.
rule.rationale: Explicit DB markers make the slow-tests boundary visible. Without them, fast tests get accidentally promoted to integration-tier latency. DB setup costs time; pure logic tests run much faster without it. --strict-markers makes missing markers a hard error.

rule.statement: DRF tests use `APIClient` + `client.force_authenticate(user=user)`. Do NOT call the login endpoint inside every test setup. Use APIClient.force_authenticate instead of issuing real login requests in integration tests — much faster and tests the endpoint, not the auth flow.
rule.rationale: force_authenticate skips the auth round-trip; tests run an order of magnitude faster and isolate the unit under test. Real login calls include password hashing and token generation — 100-1000ms per test. force_authenticate bypasses all of that.

rule.statement: Mocks live ONLY at process boundaries: outbound HTTP, S3, third-party SDKs, email. Internal services / utils are called for real (in-memory DB). Mock at the I/O boundary (HTTP, mail, payment), test the rest with real DB and real serialization. Over-mocking produces tests that prove nothing.
rule.rationale: Mocking internal services tests the mocks, not the code. Boundary-only mocking keeps tests honest while staying fast. Mocking internal methods tests implementation, not behavior. Tests that mock the wrong import path pass silently with zero real coverage.

rule.statement: Set DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE in pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] to a test-specific settings file with DEBUG=False, in-memory cache, fake email backend, and MD5PasswordHasher.
rule.rationale: Test settings reduce overhead and prevent accidental real email/payment sends. MD5PasswordHasher speeds up tests by 10-100x but must never leak into dev/prod settings.

rule.statement: Keep conftest.py close to where fixtures are used. Project-root conftest only for truly global fixtures (api_client, user, auth_client, network-blocking).
rule.rationale: Auto-discovery cascades — nested conftest fixtures shadow each other silently if not scoped.

rule.statement: Add an autouse network-blocking fixture in the root conftest that raises on any socket.create_connection call. Tests that need real network must explicitly opt out.
rule.rationale: Tests that forget to mock external services produce 30s timeouts, not clear failures. A loud guard makes the gap obvious immediately.

rule.statement: Structure each test: Arrange (set up data) → Act (call code under test) → Assert (verify observable outcome). One logical assertion group per test.
rule.rationale: Tests with multiple unrelated assertions fail for multiple reasons simultaneously, making the root cause ambiguous.

rule.statement: Use @pytest.mark.parametrize for boundary and equivalence-class testing where the same logic runs against multiple inputs.
rule.rationale: Replaces repetitive test functions with a single declaration; failures show exactly which parameter set failed.

rule.statement: Use transactional_db (not db) when the code under test calls transaction.on_commit — on_commit callbacks never fire inside a rolled-back transaction.
rule.rationale: db wraps each test in a savepoint that never commits; on_commit handlers that send emails or dispatch tasks are silently skipped.

rule.statement: Require agents to read tests/conftest.py before generating any test. Prompt: "Read tests/conftest.py first. Reuse existing fixtures."
rule.rationale: LLMs default to inline creation rather than reuse; reading the file first surfaces the available fixture names.

rule.statement: Require --strict-markers and a lint rule that finds DB-touching code in tests without @pytest.mark.django_db.
rule.rationale: LLMs omit the marker; the resulting error is clear but wastes tokens iterating. Catch it in lint, not at runtime.

rule.statement: When the project is Django 5.x or 4.2 LTS on Python 3.12+, the code lives under `apps/<app>/` or `core/`, `pytest + pytest-django` is configured and service-layer separation is agreed, the test-stack setup or migration MUST run on a named trigger - the first test module for a new `apps/<app>/`, or a CI run of `pytest --strict-markers` - and MUST produce the 02-output-contract record from the actual configuration: `runner` from `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` with `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` pinned, `factory_strategy` from `tests/factories.py` versus `baker.make` usage, `db_marker_used` from the strict-markers lint of r14, `auth_strategy` from the `authenticated_client` fixture in `tests/conftest.py`, and `boundary_mocks_only` from a scan of `mocker.patch` targets.
rule.rationale: Three of the five required fields are constants, so a record written from memory is always valid. Deriving each field from the config and the lint is what turns fm-03 (missing db marker) and fm-10 (patching the wrong import path) into a red field before the suite runs, instead of a 30-second timeout in CI.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but a required field cannot be computed - `pyproject.toml` has no `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` block or no `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` (Step 1 unfinished), `tests/conftest.py` is absent so `auth_strategy` cannot be read, or inline `.objects.create()` still coexists with `tests/factories.py` (Step 3 unfinished) - the setup MUST block naming the unfinished step and the missing prerequisite, and MUST NOT emit a record with `db_marker_used: true` before the strict-markers lint has run or `auth_strategy: force_authenticate` copied from `templates/conftest.py` rather than read from the project's own conftest.

rationale.source: pytest-django docs - Configuring Django settings; factory_boy docs

rule.rationale: Without `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` pytest-django cannot even import the models, so every downstream field is a guess. A record that claims `force_authenticate` while the tests still POST to /login (fm-04) passes the schema and hides the 100-1000 ms per test that r5 exists to remove.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - the project is not Django (FastAPI, Flask), it is a throwaway tool with no growth horizon, or the `apps/core/config` layout is not adopted and refactoring it is out of scope - the methodology MUST NOT be applied; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor (the `pyproject.toml` commit or the ticket) naming the failed precondition and the route taken instead (the framework-specific test methodology for non-Django Python; `django-coding-standards` first when the layout is the blocker), and an existing `unittest`-style `TestCase` suite MUST NOT be reported as a partial pass of this methodology.

rationale.source: pytest-django docs; Django docs - Testing tools

rule.rationale: A `TestCase` suite in a flat repo can be green in CI and still match none of these rules; only the anchored skip says whether that is a deliberate deferral or an unnoticed gap. Recording the route keeps the layout refactor and the pytest migration ordered instead of attempted at once.
